newsitem.title: UK: Japan oil spill to spread - industry body.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil spill to spread - industry body.

text.p: Oil from a Russian tanker which broke up off Japan last week will spread, an industry body said in an update on the situation on Wednesday.

"Only about one kilometre of shoreline is currently affected by the oil spill but this is likely to increase as the oil migrates along the coast," the International Tanker Owners Pollution Federation said in a statement.

The upturned bow section, which grounded close to shore near Mikuni, Japan, on January 7, may contain up to 3,000 tonnes of oil. This is gradually leaking out and being driven onshore by prevailing winds.
The initial release of some 3,000 tonnes of medium fuel oil when the tanker broke up 120 miles offshore has largely dispersed at sea due to wave action, ITOPF said.
The sunken stern section is still releasing small amounts of oil, but this is "dispersing naturally at sea and does not pose a threat to coastal resources," it added.
The 13,157-tonne Nakhodka was believed to be carrying 19,000 tonnes of C grade medium fuel oil when it got into difficulties in the Sea of Japan on January 2.
ITOPF said the tanker's owners, Prisco Traffic Limited, had contracted the Japan Disaster Prevention Centre to undertake clean-up operations.
Prisco has also obtained equipment from the Petroleum Association of Japan to collect floating oil and protect certain areas.
The UK P&I Club, the largest of the mutual marine P&I clubs, said last week it provided Protection and Indemnity insurance for the tanker. P&I insurance covers maritime pollution claims.
